transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, I suppose what brings me in is... well, I just haven't been quite myself lately. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or anything, it's just... I don't seem to have the same push I used to. 

I used to be so involved, you know? Choir practice, my quilting circle, visiting folks... but lately, I just... I haven't been going. Most days I just sit at home. I keep the TV on low, just for some noise. I know people are expecting me, and I feel terrible about it, I really do. I just can't seem to get going. Is that... is that the sort of thing you need to know? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way, not having the same push and staying at home more?

Well, um... I don't want to make a big fuss about it, but I suppose it's been building up for a little while now. Ever since I retired from the school office. That was, oh, a little over two years ago. 

It wasn't all at once, you know. Just sort of... slowly happening over time. I kept thinking I would just snap out of it and get back to my normal self, so I hope you don't mind that I waited this long to come see you. I didn't want to be a bother if it was just me being a bit slow. Does that make sense, Doctor? Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Can you describe your mood most days? Do you feel down or depressed often?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. I hope that doesn't sound strange, especially after I just told you I'm sitting at home so much these days. I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back, but I really don't sit around crying or feeling blue. 

I always try to keep a good attitude, I really do. It's more just... I don't know, feeling a bit blank or quiet, I suppose? But not down in the dumps. I wouldn't call it depressed, no. I hope that's okay to say... I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things actually are. Am I explaining that alright for you, Doctor?
Do you still enjoy the things you used to enjoy, like your quilting circle or visiting people, or has that changed lately?

Well, um... I hope you don't think I'm ungrateful for the things I have, because I really did used to love those activities. But... no, I suppose I don't really enjoy them the same way anymore. 

It's like I mentioned before, about not having that same push. I still think the quilting circle is a lovely group of ladies, and I feel just awful that I haven't been going. I know they're probably wondering where I am, and I don't want to let them down. But when the time comes to get ready and go out, I just... I don't feel that spark of looking forward to it. So I end up just staying in my chair with the TV on low. I'm not trying to be difficult or anti-social, I promise. It just feels easier to sit quietly. Is that... is that helpful for you to know, Doctor? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you find that you feel tired or like you don’t have much energy most days?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel tired, exactly. I hope I'm not making this confusing for you. My body feels perfectly fine, and I don't feel like I need to sleep all day or anything like that. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just being lazy when I say I sit in my chair so much. Physically, I have the energy to get up and do things... it's just that the, well, the urge to actually go do them just isn't there. I hope it's alright that I don't have a better way to explain it. Am I making sense, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you find it harder to focus or concentrate on things lately, like following the TV show you're watching or making small decisions?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing. I hope that's the right answer. I mean, I don't want you to think my mind is going or anything like that. 

When I sit in my chair with the TV on, I can follow the programs just fine. I might not be paying the closest attention, but that's just because I'm resting quietly, not because I can't understand what's happening. And as for making decisions, well, I don't have too many big choices to make these days, but I manage just fine with the small ones. I try my best to keep my mind sharp, I really do. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about, Doctor? I hope I'm being helpful.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in activities like your quilting circle or visiting people, or do you still care about them but just find it hard to participate?

Well, um... I really hope you don't think I'm just giving up on things, because I do still care. I care very much. I feel just terrible that I haven't been going to choir or the quilting circle, especially since I know the ladies are expecting me. 

It's not that I've lost interest completely, I promise. It's just... like I was saying before, I just don't have that push I used to have to actually get out the door. So I end up just sitting at home with the TV on low. I know I should be doing more, and I don't want you to think I'm happy just sitting there all day. It's just hard to explain why I can't seem to make myself go. I hope that makes sense, Doctor. Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Have you been feeling like you’re letting people down or feeling guilty about not participating in activities lately?

Oh, well, um... no, I wouldn't say guilty. I hope that doesn't make me sound selfish or anything. I know I just said I feel bad about missing the ladies, but it's not like a heavy guilt or feeling like I'm a bad person. 

My friends, they're very understanding, so I don't feel like I'm letting them down, exactly. I don't sit in my chair beating myself up over it. I try to keep a good, positive attitude, I really do. I just don't have that kind of guilt weighing on my mind. Is it okay that I don't feel that way, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual or, on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still lately?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I've noticed anything like that. I hope that's alright. I mean, I am getting a little older, so I might not move quite as fast as a young girl, but I get up and around just fine. I certainly don't want you to think I'm getting sluggish or lazy, because I'm really not. 

And I don't get all jittery or restless, either. Like I said before, I just sit quietly in my chair. I don't pace around the house or fidget. I try to be very calm and peaceful. Does that sound okay to you, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly or make decisions, even about small things?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. My thinking is still just fine, thank goodness. I really hope you don't think I'm getting all muddled or confused, because I'm really not. 

I can still make my own choices just fine, even if it's just deciding what to have for a little lunch or what to watch on the television. I try very hard to keep my thoughts straight so I don't cause a fuss or become a burden to anybody. I'm still doing okay up here, I promise. Is that what you needed to know, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right information.
Would you say that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even a little bit?

Oh, well, um... no, I wouldn't say that at all. I still find joy in my days, I really do. I hope you don't think I'm ungrateful or just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I'm definitely not doing that. 

I still enjoy a nice hot cup of tea in the morning, or... or just looking out the window at the birds in the yard. Just the simple things, you know? I always try to appreciate what I have and keep a smile on my face. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm a gloomy person. Does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like waking up much earlier than usual and not being able to fall back asleep?

Oh, well, um... no, my sleep has been just fine, thank you for asking. I usually sleep right through the night. I really hope that's okay. 

I know some folks my age wake up at the crack of dawn and can't get back to sleep, but I try very hard to get a full night's rest. I wouldn't want you to think I'm up all hours of the night causing a racket or anything like that, because I'm definitely not. I just stay in bed quietly until it's a proper time to get up, like I'm supposed to. 

I hope I'm being helpful with these answers, Doctor. Am I doing okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy a lot?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say I've lost interest completely, no. I still care about things, I really do. It's just... well, I suppose what brings me in today is that I just don't seem to have the push I used to have. Like for my choir, or my quilting, or going out to visit folks. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy, because I'm really not trying to be. But most days lately, I just end up sitting at home with the television on low... even though I know people are expecting me. I feel just awful about letting them down, and I'd hate for anyone to think badly of me. I try to be good and do what I'm supposed to do, I really do. 

Is it alright that I told you that, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way and being a good help to you.
Would you say that you’ve stopped taking much pleasure in most of the things you used to enjoy, even the ones you really liked before?

Oh, well, um... no, I wouldn't say I've stopped taking pleasure in things. I think... well, I think we might have just talked about this, didn't we? I really hope I'm not repeating myself and wasting your time, Doctor. 

Like I said before, I still enjoy my tea and watching the birds. I still like those things very much. It's just the... the bigger things, like choir, that I don't have the energy for right now. But I certainly haven't stopped liking them. I wouldn't want you to think I've just given up on everything, because I promise I haven't. I'm trying very hard to stay positive. 

Did I explain that alright this time? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not confusing things.
Would you say that you’ve completely stopped doing most of the things you used to enjoy, even if you still care about them deep down?

Oh, well, um... no, I wouldn't say I've completely stopped everything. I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, Doctor. I know we just talked about my choir and the quilting... 

I try my best to keep up with the little things, like I mentioned. I still make my bed every morning and water my plants. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just letting everything go to ruin, because I'm definitely not. I'm trying to be a good housekeeper still. 

It's just... maybe I'm doing a bit less of the social things, but I certainly haven't stopped doing everything. I hope that makes sense? I really want to be sure I'm understanding what you're asking and giving you the right answers. Am I doing okay?
Would you say that you’ve been less interested in doing things you used to enjoy, even if you still care about them?

Oh, my... I'm so sorry, Doctor. I feel just terrible. I must not be explaining myself very well at all if you have to keep asking me about this. I really don't mean to be a difficult patient... 

But no, I wouldn't say I'm less interested. The interest is still right there in my heart, I promise you. I still want to do all my usual things, and I care about them just as much as I ever did. It's just like I was saying before, about not always having the get-up-and-go... but the interest itself hasn't gone anywhere. 

I really hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same sort of answer. Am I doing this wrong? I just want to make sure I'm understanding you properly and being a good patient for you.
Would you say that you’ve had a marked decrease in interest in most activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, Doctor. I feel like I'm making a mess of things, with you having to ask me this again. I really am trying my best to answer you properly, I promise. 

But... no, I wouldn't say there's been a marked decrease in my interest. That sounds so... so final, doesn't it? Like I've just given up. And I haven't, I really haven't. I still care very much about my choir and my quilting and my garden. I still want to be involved and do all those things. 

It's just... well, sometimes it's hard to get started, you know? But the interest is absolutely still there. I really hope I'm not being difficult by saying no again. I just want to be truthful with you. Are my answers helping at all? I'd hate to think I'm wasting your time when you're trying to help me.
Would you say that you’ve felt down or had little pleasure in doing things for most of the day, more days than not, in the past two weeks?

Oh, goodness, no... I wouldn't say that at all. I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, Doctor, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for... 

But no, I haven't been feeling down like that. I mean, everyone has a quiet day here and there, don't they? But most of the day, more days than not? Oh, no. I still find plenty of joy in my day-to-day routine. Like I said, I still tend to my plants and keep the house tidy. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping, because I'm really not. 

I try to keep a positive outlook, I really do. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing. Am I being helpful, Doctor?
Would you say that you’ve had a low mood or lost interest in most activities for most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years or more?

Oh, my... two years? No, no, definitely not. I'm so sorry, Doctor, I feel like I'm just being so repetitive and I really don't want to frustrate you... 

But no, I haven't been low or lost interest for years like that. Goodness, that sounds so dreadful, doesn't it? Like a person wouldn't even be trying anymore. And I always try my best to keep busy and keep a smile on, I really do. I still have my little routines and things that bring me joy. 

I really hope it's okay that I keep saying no to these questions. I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything from you, I promise. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I doing okay? I just want to be a good patient for you and help you figure this all out.
